newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Samancor dips to low after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Samancor dips to low after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Samancor Ltd dipped to a new year low on Thursday following a profit warning from the firm on Wednesday, dealers said.
The firm's stock fell 155 cents to end at 45.50 rand, well below the previous low of 47.00 rand.
"The warning knocked things off a lot. It was unexpected, but volumes have been light," one dealer said.
Just more than 156,000 shares changed hands during the day.

Samancor warned after the market had shut on Wednesday that its operating profit for its second half would slump and the firm would fail to meet a previous forecast that they would be similar to those in the first half.
"It is now clear that this forecast will not be achieved," it said.
However, the announcement came with a statement it had sold its 50 percent interest in graphite electrode manufacturer EMSA to its joint venture partner UCAR International Inc for 335 million rand.
The firm said the proceeds of the sale would offset the operating profit fall and second half attributable profits would exceed those of the first half.
"The news on the sale may be providing some support (for the share price)," the dealer added.
